title: Sea-urchin larvae reared without lime develop healthily but lack skeletal rods and arms

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Sea-urchin larvae reared without lime develop healthily but lack skeletal rods and arms

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Sea-urchin eggs reared in lime-free sea-water develop into apparently healthy larvae that lack the calcareous skeletal rods, and the long larval arms normally supported by those rods are suppressed; the organism can live without the material of its skeleton.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the eggs of sea-urchins reared in lime-free water develop in apparent health, into larvae entirely destitute of the usual skeleton of calcareous rods, and in which, accordingly, the long arms of the Pluteus larva, which the rods support and distend, are entirely suppressed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Development without skeletal material”. Scope: echinoid pluteus larvae (and by extension skeleton-forming organisms deprived of skeletal material)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The treatment and outcomes give a clean experimental test with standard analysis. Public experimental records and images may test some species, but existence of sufficiently documented lime-free experiments is uncertain and the extension beyond echinoids is not covered.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare survival, developmental stage, skeletal-rod mineralization and arm length between control and calcium-depleted sea-urchin larvae. The claim is supported by viable stage-matched larvae lacking rods and long arms specifically under calcium depletion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Lime-free water can cause physiological effects beyond skeleton loss.

A dedicated open replication dataset may not exist.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Rods, arms and survival are an obvious confirming and refuting pattern, and the contrast with seawater controls is discriminating. The observations exist in the experimental literature, including later repeats of calcium-free culture, but they are not gathered in a public dataset that can be reanalysed as data. A literature compilation can test the claim for the species that were reared and cannot underwrite the broader extension.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In published lime-free versus normal seawater rearings of echinoid embryos, score skeletal-rod presence, larval-arm length and survival. Suppression of rods and arms with continued development supports the claim; normal skeletons, or death rather than skeleton-less development, refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Apparently healthy is loosely defined, and the published experiments cover a few echinoid species rather than skeleton-forming organisms generally.

The rearings are reported as figures in papers, not as a reusable open table of larvae, treatments and phenotypes.
